source: Wempe's works drawings (References/wempe/drawings/), by drawing number; P1a, 14 October 2026: the frame (group 05 08), from References/wempe/transcriptions/05-08-frame.md checked on the sheets; P1b: the going train (group 05 05, 05-05-05-02-train-motionwork.md) and its bearings; P1d: the balance and escapement (groups 05 03, 05 04), from 05-03-05-04-balance-escapement.md checked on the sheets, the jewels by the coloured section's labels; P1c: the fusee, maintaining work, barrel, mainspring, chain and band (groups 05 06, 05 07 and 05 05 05, 05-06-05-07-fusee-barrel.md); P1e: the dial, motion work, hands and up-and-down work (group 05 02), from 05-05-05-02-train-motionwork.md checked on the sheets, the up-and-down pinion's and the seconds collet's numbers by the coloured section's labels. Each line's id is its drawing number without the spaces (050800-1 for 05 08 00-1, as 05 09 01's title block writes its own), since a piece's lines are a space-separated list; a Wempe standard part by its WN number, with a suffix where one number is on several lines, or a name where its number isn't read. 'no' is left empty: bom.py's registry matches a card's numbers against it, and the drawing numbers are not of its form; P1f: the case and box (groups 05 01 and 51 00, 05-01-51-00-case-box-overview.md, checked on the sheets), a part without a number by a name

relations.in: the part's axis inside the named part: tap (thread in a tapped hole), clear (through a clearance hole), run, free, press (as the Hamilton's bom.json)
relations.round: the part's bore round the named part
relations.on: rests against the named part (surfaces within 0.02 mm)
relations.mesh: teeth engage: centre distance m(z1+z2)/2, the same module, the faces overlapping, turning in the tooth ratio (as the Hamilton's bom.json)
relations.endshake: axial play between the named bearings (bom.py's 0.025-0.076 mm, the Hamilton's; the Wempe's sheets give none: their arbors' and bushes' tolerances give 0.05-0.12)

lines.name: Unterplatte (pillar plate)
lines.fn: The lower plate, under the dial: the foundation of the movement (its assembly, Unterplatte kompl., is 05 08 02).

lines.name: Oberplatte (top plate)
lines.fn: The upper plate, on the train side (its sheet's title block numbers it 05 09 01; its assembly, Oberplatte kompl., is 05 08 01).

lines.name: Pfeiler (pillar)
lines.fn: Hold the plates 19 mm apart, their shoulders in seats in the plates, their spigots in the plates' reamed holes.

lines.name: Pillar screw, dial side (WN-56, by the coloured section's label)
lines.fn: Hold each pillar to the pillar plate, from the dial side.

lines.name: Pillar screw, train side (WN-57, by the coloured section's label)
lines.fn: Hold the top plate to each pillar, from its outer face.

lines.name: Werkring (movement ring)
lines.fn: The ring the pillar plate sits in, which carries the dial and hangs in the case.

lines.name: Movement ring screw (WN number not read)
lines.fn: Its head bears on the pillar plate's rim and holds it in the ring's seat.

lines.name: Stellstift (WN-201): the plate's pin in the movement ring
lines.fn: Drilled across the joint of the pillar plate and the ring at assembly, it sets the movement's turn in the ring.

lines.name: Federhausbrücke (barrel bridge)
lines.fn: Holds the barrel arbor's upper pivot over the top plate's cut (its assembly is 05 08 05).

lines.name: Sperrkegel (click)
lines.fn: The click on the barrel's ratchet, spring-hard brass, its own spring.

lines.name: Click screw, shouldered (WN-22)
lines.fn: The click turns on its shoulder.

lines.name: Barrel bridge screw (WN-55, by the coloured section's label)
lines.fn: Hold the barrel bridge to the top plate.

lines.name: Stellstift (WN-203), barrel bridge
lines.fn: Place the barrel bridge on the top plate.

lines.name: Schneckenfutter (fusee bush)
lines.fn: Its spigot slides into the top plate's hole (8 g6 in 8.0 +0.015) and its flange is screwed to it: the fusee arbor's winding end turns in it.

lines.name: Fusee bush screw (WN-34)
lines.fn: Hold the fusee bush's flange to the top plate.

lines.name: Staubfutter (dust bush)
lines.fn: Pressed on the fusee bush's tapered top (8 H7 on 8 T6, both 1:70), up to the case's winding hole.

lines.name: Korkring (cork ring)
lines.fn: Pressed on the dust bush's neck, on its collar, standing 0.95 over it: the case's closing plate meets it round the winding hole, keeping dust out (no sheet; scaled on the coloured section).

lines.name: Unruhkloben oben (upper balance cock)
lines.fn: Holds the balance staff's upper jewel setting over the top plate.

lines.name: Upper balance cock screw (hole 8; WN-55 by the coloured section's label)
lines.fn: Holds the upper cock to the top plate.

lines.name: Stellstift, upper balance cock (holes 6, 9, 50; WN not given, as WN-203)
lines.fn: Place the upper cock on the top plate.

lines.name: Unruhkloben unten (lower balance cock)
lines.fn: Hangs under the top plate and holds the balance staff's lower jewel setting.

lines.name: Lower balance cock screw (WN-53, by the coloured section's label)
lines.fn: From the top plate's outer face, its head sunk in the plate, into the cock.

lines.name: Stellstift, lower balance cock (holes 22, 37; WN not given, as WN-203)
lines.fn: Place the lower cock under the top plate.

lines.name: Zwischenbrücke (intermediate bridge; its sheet not in the set, the assembly 05 08 04)
lines.fn: On the pillar plate's dial side: the intermediate wheel's lower jewel and the seconds wheel's lower setting.

lines.name: Intermediate bridge screw (WN-52)
lines.fn: Hold the intermediate bridge to the pillar plate, from the dial side.

lines.name: Stellstift (WN-203), intermediate bridge
lines.fn: Place the intermediate bridge on the pillar plate.

lines.name: Minutenrad kompl. (centre wheel complete)
lines.fn: The centre arbor: its wheel riveted on its pinion and arbor (22.7.43).

lines.name: Minutentrieb (centre pinion and arbor)
lines.fn: Driven by the fusee wheel; turns once an hour; runs in the top plate's bush WN-301 and, by its journal, in the pillar plate's WN-302, and carries the cannon tube (05 05 03-3) on its shank.

dev.why: the train-side shoulder is one 30° cone from the pivot's root (05 05 03-2), so it bears on the jewel at its hole's edge, 0.014 up the cone from where a flat shoulder bore (26 October 2026): 0.084 in all, inside the Wempe's own band for the centre arbor, the 1958 Soviet MX repair book's 0.07-0.10 (Appendix 4; wempe_bench.js), over the Hamilton manual's 0.003 in this check takes

lines.name: Minutenrad (centre wheel)
lines.fn: Riveted on the pinion's seat; drives the intermediate pinion.

lines.name: Zwischenrad kompl. (intermediate wheel complete)
lines.fn: The intermediate (third) arbor: its wheel riveted on its pinion and arbor (27.7.40).

lines.name: Zwischentrieb (intermediate pinion and arbor)
lines.fn: Driven by the centre wheel; runs in the top plate's bush WN-300 and the intermediate bridge's. In the Soviet 6MX (the page's Variants) it runs in jewels in chatons at both ends.

dev.why: in the Soviet 6MX the train-side shoulder's 30° cone (its sheet) sits into the 6MX's own upper jewel's wider mouth, so it bears 0.073 from the jewel's face where a flat shoulder bore about 0.03 (26 October 2026): 0.103 in all, 0.003 over the 1958 Soviet MX repair book's 0.07-0.10 for it (Appendix 4; wempe_bench.js): reported, the 6MX's jewels' mouths not measured on a source; over the Hamilton manual's 0.003 in this check takes

lines.name: Zwischenrad (intermediate wheel)
lines.fn: Riveted on the pinion's seat; drives the seconds pinion.

lines.name: Sekundenrad kompl. (seconds wheel complete)
lines.fn: The seconds (fourth) arbor: its wheel riveted on its pinion and arbor (27.7.40).

lines.name: Sekundentrieb (seconds pinion and arbor)
lines.fn: Driven by the intermediate wheel; turns once a minute; runs in the top plate's bush WN-300 and the jewel 05 05 04-1 in the intermediate bridge; its lower pivot goes on as the seconds hand's post. In the Soviet 6MX its upper pivot runs in a jewel in a chaton.

dev.why: in the Soviet 6MX the train-side shoulder's 30° cone (its sheet) sits into the 6MX's own upper jewel's wider mouth, so it bears 0.068 from the jewel's face where a flat shoulder bore about 0.03 (26 October 2026): 0.093 in all, inside the 1958 Soviet MX repair book's 0.07-0.10 for it (Appendix 4; wempe_bench.js); over the Hamilton manual's 0.003 in this check takes

lines.name: Sekundenrad (seconds wheel)
lines.fn: Riveted on the pinion's seat; drives the escape pinion (05 04 05-2).

lines.name: Messinglager WN-301 (brass bush, centre arbor's upper pivot)
lines.fn: The centre arbor's upper bearing, pressed into the top plate's hole 1.

lines.name: Messinglager WN-300 (brass bush, intermediate arbor's upper pivot)
lines.fn: The intermediate arbor's upper bearing, pressed into the top plate's hole 38.

lines.name: Messinglager WN-300 (brass bush, seconds arbor's upper pivot)
lines.fn: The seconds arbor's upper bearing, pressed into the top plate's hole 35.

lines.name: Messinglager WN-302 (brass bush, centre arbor's journal)
lines.fn: The centre arbor's lower bearing, pressed into the pillar plate's hole 1, 0.1 under its inner face.

lines.name: Messinglager WN-300 (brass bush, intermediate arbor's lower pivot)
lines.fn: The intermediate arbor's lower bearing, pressed into the intermediate bridge, 0.7 in from its plate side.

lines.name: Chaton (6MX), intermediate arbor's upper jewel
lines.fn: Holds the intermediate arbor's upper jewel in the top plate's hole 38, where the drawings press the bush WN-300. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's (Altmeppen; Kirov No. 247's photographs), its sizes estimated.

lines.name: Hole jewel (6MX), intermediate arbor, upper
lines.fn: The intermediate arbor's upper pivot runs in it; its face takes the arbor's shoulder. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's (Altmeppen; Kirov No. 247's photographs), its sizes estimated.

lines.name: Chaton (6MX), seconds arbor's upper jewel
lines.fn: Holds the seconds arbor's upper jewel in the top plate's hole 35, where the drawings press the bush WN-300. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's (Altmeppen; Kirov No. 247's photographs), its sizes estimated.

lines.name: Hole jewel (6MX), seconds arbor, upper
lines.fn: The seconds arbor's upper pivot runs in it; its face takes the arbor's shoulder. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's (Altmeppen; Kirov No. 247's photographs), its sizes estimated.

lines.name: Chaton (6MX), intermediate arbor's lower jewel
lines.fn: Holds the intermediate arbor's lower jewel in the intermediate bridge, where the drawings press the bush WN-300. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's (Altmeppen; Kirov No. 247's photographs), its sizes estimated.

lines.name: Hole jewel (6MX), intermediate arbor, lower
lines.fn: The intermediate arbor's lower pivot runs in it; its face takes the arbor's shoulder. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's (Altmeppen; Kirov No. 247's photographs), its sizes estimated.

lines.name: Fassung (the seconds jewel's setting)
lines.fn: Holds the seconds arbor's lower jewel in the intermediate bridge (its sheet isn't in the set; the coloured section names it).

lines.name: Lagerstein f. Sek. (the seconds arbor's lower jewel)
lines.fn: The seconds arbor's lower pivot runs in it; its face takes the arbor's endshake (its sheet isn't in the set; the coloured section names it).

lines.name: Futter (stud bush)
lines.fn: Pressed into the pillar plate from its inner face at holes 2 and 19, holding the motion work's studs (the one at 19 drawn dashed on 05 08 02: estimated).

lines.name: Bush in hole 18, the hand-setting pinion's (not named on 05 08 02)
lines.fn: The bearing of the hand-setting work's pinion (Zeigerstelltrieb), pressed into the pillar plate's hole 18; on Wempe 3955 the only part of that work fitted, empty.

lines.name: Anrichtstift lg (long stud)
lines.fn: The up-and-down wheel's stud, at hole 2, 12.3 long from the plate's inner face.

lines.name: Anrichtstift kurz (short stud)
lines.fn: The motion work's change wheel's stud, at hole 19, 6.8 out of the plate's dial face.

lines.name: Unruhreifen (balance rim with arm, nickel steel and brass)
lines.fn: The cut bimetallic rim and its arm, on the hub of the staff.

dev.why: as first drawn (the page's Variants) the arm is riveted on the 1941 collar's neck (05 04_5), which stands between its hole and the staff: the 1946 staff's seat Ø 2 h6 isn't there

lines.name: Masse (compensation mass)
lines.fn: Round brass masses across the rim, which the rim carries in as it warms.

lines.name: Schraube (WN-12), the mass screw
lines.fn: Holds a mass on the rim: M0.8 (estimated) radially through its outer jaw's tapped hole, its head in a counterbore in the mass's round side, its tip on the rim's outer face (05 03_2; the 6MX's book, Fig. 5.62).

lines.name: Schraube (WN-12a), for the tapped hole in a mass's top (not fitted)
lines.fn: For the tapped hole M1.2 in the middle of a mass's top, its top flat (not fitted: holes in all four, empty, the owner's choice, 28 October 2026): the coloured section draws one, a cheese head on one mass; Wempe's lever 2965 and the earlier 2493 show such holes empty; the Einheits examples photographed (Wempe 3955, the Langes) have plain tops (a poising screw fitted where needed).

lines.name: Zeitschraube (timing screw)
lines.fn: Across the rim at the arm's end in its tapped hole Ø 0.9 × 0.16, carrying the timing weight.

lines.name: Zeitmasse (timing weight)
lines.fn: On the timing screw: turned in or out, sets the rate.

lines.name: Unruhwelle (balance staff)
lines.fn: The balance staff, its pivots in the jewels of the two cocks. As last revised 05 04 02 (29.5.46); as first drawn (the page's Variants) 05 04_5's staff of 4.4.41, which carries this number in pencil.

lines.name: Unruhbutzen (balance hub, brass)
lines.fn: Pressed on the staff, its flange carries the arm. As first drawn (the page's Variants) 05 04_5's brass collar (040401-2), the arm riveted on its neck, with no screws.

lines.name: Schraube (WN-10), the hub's screws
lines.fn: From the arm's top, their countersunk heads flush in it, through the arm's Ø 1 into the hub's flange, tapped M1 (05 04 02, the coloured section). Only on the 1946 hub: the 1941 collar has no holes for them.

lines.name: Spiralfeder (helical hairspring)
lines.fn: The balance spring: 13 turns between its two terminal curves.

lines.name: Spiralrolle (hairspring collet)
lines.fn: On the staff's 1:70 seat; the spring's inner end pinned in the hole across its end.

lines.name: Spiralstift (hairspring pin, at the collet)
lines.fn: Wedges the spring's inner end in the collet's hole (Ø 0.8, Kegel 1:90): half round, brass, its flat on the strip, as the stud's pin holds the outer end (its form estimated from the stud's).

lines.name: Klötzchen (hairspring stud)
lines.fn: On the cock, its upright through the cock's slot, holding the spring's outer end.

lines.name: Stift (hairspring pin, at the stud)
lines.fn: Wedges the spring's outer end in the stud's hole (Ø 0.7, drilled at assembly, 3.15 under the bar), as the collet's pin holds the inner end.

lines.name: Schraube (WN-11), the stud's screw
lines.fn: Holds the stud to the cock.

lines.name: Heberolle (impulse roller, beryllium copper; 05 04 03-1 in the coloured section)
lines.fn: Carries the impulse stone, which the escape wheel pushes.

lines.name: Hebestein (impulse stone, sapphire)
lines.fn: Receives the escape wheel's impulse.

lines.name: Auslöserolle (discharge roller)
lines.fn: Carries the discharge stone.

lines.name: Auslösestein (discharge stone)
lines.fn: Lifts the detent through the gold spring on one swing; passes it on the other.

lines.name: Gangrad (escape wheel, 15 teeth)
lines.fn: Locked on the detent's stone between impulses, it gives the balance its impulse.

lines.name: Gangtrieb (escape pinion, z 10, m 0.263, and arbor)
lines.fn: The arbor and pinion; driven by the seconds wheel. As first drawn (the page's Variants) 05 04_7.1's arbor of 4.4.41 (050408 bis 10, renumbered 05 04 05 on 05 04_7.2), the wheel 1.4 nearer the top plate.

lines.name: Gangradbutzen (escape wheel collet; 05 04 10 on 05 04_7.2)
lines.fn: The brass collet the wheel is pressed on. As first drawn 05 04_7.1's: a cone Ø 3.0, then a pipe Ø 1.8 to 5 over the wheel.

lines.name: Gangfeder (spring detent, drawing 1436)
lines.fn: Holds the escape wheel on its locking stone; lifted on one swing by the discharge stone through the gold spring.

lines.name: Ruhestein (locking stone)
lines.fn: Locks each tooth of the escape wheel: Ø 0.75 in the detent's pipe, ground half away below it.

lines.name: Goldfeder (gold passing spring)
lines.fn: Screwed to the detent, resting on its horn: the discharge stone lifts the detent through it on one swing and bends it aside on the other.

lines.name: Schraube (WN-14), the gold spring's screw
lines.fn: Holds the gold spring to the detent's square.

dev.why: the detent's square is 0.50 thick across (0.55 as first drawn: 05 04 01-1), so the gold spring's M0.7 screw engages 0.39 of its tapped hole, 0.42 deep (the sheet gives no depth), under this check's 0.4: all the square has

lines.name: Detent foot screw, M1 (WN-13 by the coloured section's label, likely)
lines.fn: Clamps the detent's foot to the block's end.

lines.name: Stellstift (WN-205 by the coloured section's label), the detent's foot pins
lines.fn: Place the detent's foot on the block.

lines.name: Gangfederkloben (detent block)
lines.fn: Under the top plate, carries the detent. As first drawn (05 04_1, Wempe 3955), a base with a long arm and its banking screw in place of the upright.

lines.name: Detent block screw, M1.7 (WN-15 by the coloured section's label, likely)
lines.fn: From the top plate's outer face through hole 13 into the block. The Soviet 6MX's: a slotted stud flush in the plate's outer face, 2.2 from hole 13 (Kirov No. 247), through the adjusting slide into the block.

lines.name: Screw across the block's slit upright, M1.2 (its WN number not read)
lines.fn: The Soviet 6MX's banking screw across its upright, in its tapped hole (cut 28 October 2026; as last revised until 27 October 2026, a plain shank across the slit end, bearing on nothing).

lines.name: Banking screw M1.2 along the 1943 block's slit upright, its domed slotted head (the escapement of 1943; its WN number not read)
lines.fn: Along the upright's slit end, the slit gripping its thread; its head's underside bears on the detent's pipe and sets the depth of lock. The thread from the block's sheet (M1.2), its head measured on Kirow DEC 422's, DEC 479's and Lange No. 5177's photographs, its length the 6MX's loose block's. As last revised too since 27 October 2026 (Wempe 9166; the 1946 staff read again).

lines.name: Anschlagschraube 1941 (the 1941 block's banking screw, domed head and pointed tail; WN-16 by the coloured section's label)
lines.fn: Through the 1941 block's arm on the stone's line, held by its slit end; the detent's pipe banks on its head's face, and turning it sets the depth of lock (the page's Variants, As first drawn).

lines.name: Stellstift (WN-201, "Stellstift 2" by the coloured section's label), the detent block's steady pins Ø 0.9
lines.fn: Place the block on the top plate.

lines.name: Adjusting slide (6MX), the detent block's
lines.fn: A gilt key flush in a notch across the corner of the block's plate face and free side, the fixing stud through it. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's (a loose 6MX block photographed by Altmeppen, Kirov No. 247's in place), its sizes measured on the loose block, how it works not seen.

lines.name: Detent foot's stop screw (6MX), in the block's side
lines.fn: A large slotted screw in the block's free side beside the detent's foot, its head over the end face: a stop for the foot along the block. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's (every 6MX detent photograph), its thread estimated.

lines.name: Fassung (endstone setting), balance, upper
lines.fn: Holds the upper endstone in the cock.

lines.name: Deckstein (endstone), balance, upper
lines.fn: Stops the staff's upper pivot end.

lines.name: Fassung (jewel setting), balance, upper
lines.fn: Holds the upper hole jewel in the cock, its flange in the sink below.

lines.name: Lagerstein (hole jewel), balance, upper
lines.fn: The staff's upper pivot runs in it.

lines.name: Schraube (WN-55 by the coloured section), the upper endstone's screws, M1.2
lines.fn: Hold the endstone's setting, their heads over its edge.

lines.name: Fassung (jewel setting), balance, lower
lines.fn: Holds the lower hole jewel in the lug of the lower cock.

lines.name: Lagerstein (hole jewel), balance, lower
lines.fn: The staff's lower pivot runs in it.

lines.name: Fassung (endstone setting), balance, lower
lines.fn: Holds the lower endstone.

lines.name: Deckstein (endstone), balance, lower
lines.fn: Stops the staff's lower pivot end.

lines.name: Schraube (WN-10 by the coloured section's label, its last digit 0 or 8: likely 10), the lower settings' screws, M1.2
lines.fn: Hold the lower settings in the lug.

lines.name: Fassung (endstone setting), escape wheel, upper
lines.fn: Holds the upper endstone in the top plate's seat.

lines.name: Deckstein (endstone), escape wheel, upper
lines.fn: Stops the escape arbor's upper pivot end.

lines.name: Fassung (jewel setting), escape wheel, upper
lines.fn: Holds the upper hole jewel, flush with the top plate's inner face.

lines.name: Lagerstein (hole jewel), escape wheel, upper
lines.fn: The escape arbor's upper pivot (Ø 0.24) runs in it.

lines.name: Escape endstone screws, upper, M1.2 (their WN number not read)
lines.fn: Put in from outside: hold the upper endstone's setting, their heads over its spigot's edge (Wempe 3955).

lines.name: Fassung (jewel bush), escape wheel, lower
lines.fn: Pressed into the pillar plate's hole 26, holding the lower hole jewel.

lines.name: Lagerstein (hole jewel), escape wheel, lower
lines.fn: The escape arbor's lower pivot runs in it.

lines.name: Fassung (endstone cap), escape wheel, lower
lines.fn: On the pillar plate's dial side, holding the lower endstone.

lines.name: Deckstein (endstone), escape wheel, lower
lines.fn: Stops the escape arbor's lower pivot end.

lines.name: Escape endstone screws, lower, M1.2 (their WN number not read)
lines.fn: Hold the lower endstone's setting in its seat, their heads over its rim (Wempe 3955).

lines.name: Schnecke kompl. (the fusee, complete)
lines.fn: The fusee with its wheel, maintaining work, Vorreiber, cover plate and dust plate (15.3.41, revised 1944).

lines.name: Schnecke (the fusee: body on its arbor)
lines.fn: The body pressed on the arbor, the click wheel screwed to its large end (revised 2.3.48).

lines.name: Schneckenkörper (fusee body)
lines.fn: The cone with its nine-turn groove, pressed on the arbor's collar.

lines.name: Schneckenwelle (fusee arbor)
lines.fn: Runs in the pillar plate (its dial-side pivot) and the fusee bush (its journal); its square takes the key.

lines.name: Schneckensperrrad (click wheel)
lines.fn: On the body's large end, in its recess: drives the maintaining clicks.

lines.name: Schraube WN-19 (click wheel screw)
lines.fn: Holds the click wheel to the body; its head flush in the wheel's 1:8 hole, its thread in the body's M2, 6 +0.5 deep from the large end's recess floor (05 06 04-2).

lines.name: Kettenstift (chain pin)
lines.fn: Across the flange's slot in its hole through both ribs ("0,55∅ +0,01", 05 06 04-2): the chain's (or band's) top hook takes it.

lines.name: Deckplatte (cover plate)
lines.fn: On the arbor's step against the body's small end, over the stop bar.

lines.name: Schraube WN-20 (cover plate screw)
lines.fn: Countersunk in the cover plate, into the body's M1.7, 6 deep from the small end's recess floor (05 06 04-2).

lines.name: Vorreiber
lines.fn: Pinned on the arbor's taper under the fusee wheel, its flange in the wheel's underside recess.

lines.name: Vorreiberstift (Vorreiber pin)
lines.fn: One taper pin through the Vorreiber's hub and the arbor's cross hole, reamed through both together at the fusee's assembly (05 06 04-1: "1,1 bohren + konisch reiben"; the Vorreiber's drilled Ø 0.8, 05 06 00-2; 05 06_1 draws it Ø 1.2): drawn Ø 1.16 in the two holes' Ø 1.15, its rounded ends standing 0.4 out of the hub, as the coloured section draws it.

lines.name: Staubplatte (dust plate)
lines.fn: On the winding square, inside the dust bush.

lines.name: Schneckenrad (fusee wheel)
lines.fn: Loose on the arbor's seat, driven by the maintaining spring; drives the centre pinion.

lines.name: Gegensperrrad kompl. (maintaining ratchet, complete)
lines.fn: The ratchet with its two clicks, their screws, springs and pins.

lines.name: Gegensperrrad (maintaining ratchet)
lines.fn: Turns on the fusee wheel's tube; the maintaining detent rides on its teeth.

lines.name: Sperrkegel (click)
lines.fn: In the ratchet's cup, on its screw's shoulder; the click wheel drives it.

lines.name: Schraube WN-21 (click screw)
lines.fn: Put in from under the ratchet, threaded in its M1.7; the click turns on its shoulder.

lines.name: Sperrfeder (click spring)
lines.fn: Pinned inside the cup's wall, pressing its click onto the click wheel.

lines.name: Stift (click spring pin)
lines.fn: A rivet (the coloured section's "Niet"): through the cup's wall and the spring's hole (its Ø 0.6 holes cut through the cup, 26 October 2026), headed both sides (05 06 02: domed, about 0.2 high).

lines.name: Gegenfeder (maintaining spring)
lines.fn: An open ring between the fusee wheel and the ratchet, in the wheel's recess on its web: carries the drive.

lines.name: Stellstift f. Gegenfeder (maintaining spring's pin)
lines.fn: Pressed in the spring's holes: one into the fusee wheel, one into the ratchet.

lines.name: Gegensperrkegel kompl. (maintaining detent, complete)
lines.fn: The detent staked on its arbor (2.4.41).

lines.name: Gegensperrkegel (maintaining detent)
lines.fn: Rides on the maintaining ratchet's teeth; holds it while the chronometer is wound.

lines.name: Gegensperrwelle (its arbor)
lines.fn: Runs in the plates' holes 4 (drilled 0.9).

lines.name: Schraube (WN-27 by the coloured section's label, likely: the maintaining detent's wire spring's stud)
lines.fn: A slotted cheese-head stud screwed into the top plate's hole 5 ("Drahtfeder", M1.7) from its outer face; the wire spring is held in its end under the plate (no sheet; the coloured section draws it, the north-side photographs show it).

lines.name: Feder (the maintaining detent's wire spring)
lines.fn: A straight steel wire hanging from its stud past the detent's back: bent out by the detent, it presses the detent onto the maintaining ratchet's teeth (no sheet in the set; the coloured section names it, 05 06_4 marks its "Drahtfedermitte").

lines.name: Stellungssteg (stop bar)
lines.fn: Slides in the slot across the fusee's small end (cut in the body: 1.5 deep, 1.1 toward its upper end, which is thinner), on the cover plate; its spring holds it out, the chain on the top turn presses it in, and its upper end meets the stop pin at full wind.

lines.name: Stift (05 06 04-4: the coloured section's label and 05 06 04's parts list, likely), the stop bar's spring's pin
lines.fn: Along the slot in the body's hole 0.5 H7 (05 06 04-2), from the recess out through the end, standing into the recess through the spring's hole, which it holds.

lines.name: Stift (05 06 03-2, the coloured section's label), the stop bar's pin, on which its spring's end bears
lines.fn: Pressed across the bar near its lower end in its Ø 0.5 hole (05 06_4's C-D, dashed across the bar), standing 0.9 out of its near side, where the bar's spring's end bears.

lines.name: Stegfeder (the stop bar's spring)
lines.fn: A strip in the small end's recess, held on its pin 05 06 04-4 through a hole in it where it lies on the wall, round the wall and the bar's upper side to a free span whose end bears on the bar's pin 05 06 03-2 near the bar's lower end: holds the bar out toward that end (no sheet: drawn as 05 06_4's C-D draws it).

lines.name: Anschlagstift (stop pin)
lines.fn: Pressed in the top plate's hole 7, standing out under it: the stop bar meets it at full wind.

lines.name: Federhaus mit Deckel (barrel)
lines.fn: The drum, its lid and the spring's hook block (revised 20.4.48).

lines.name: Federhaustrommel (barrel drum)
lines.fn: Turns on the arbor's journals; the chain winds onto it.

lines.name: Federhausdeckel (barrel lid)
lines.fn: Sprung into the drum's seat on the bridge's side; turns on the arbor's upper journal.

lines.name: Federhaushaken (spring hook block)
lines.fn: Riveted inside the drum's wall: takes the mainspring's outer end.

lines.name: Steg (spring brace)
lines.fn: Stands inside the drum's wall from its bottom to its lid, its ends through the bottom's slot and the lid's notch: the mainspring's outer coil threaded between it and the wall.

lines.name: Federkern kompl. (barrel arbor, complete)
lines.fn: The arbor with its hook (28.1.43).

lines.name: Federkern (barrel arbor)
lines.fn: Runs in the pillar plate and the barrel bridge; held by the set-up ratchet and click.

lines.name: Federhaken (arbor hook)
lines.fn: Pressed in the core's hole (Ø 2 × 6, 0207): takes the mainspring's inner end.

lines.name: Sperrad (set-up ratchet)
lines.fn: On the arbor's square above the barrel bridge; the bridge's click holds it.

lines.name: Zugfeder (mainspring)
lines.fn: In the drum: inner end on the arbor's hook, outer end on the drum's block. Its length isn't drawn: estimated.

lines.name: Kette (fusee chain)
lines.fn: Between the barrel and the fusee: its top hook on the fusee's pin, its bottom hook in the drum's slot (the page's default; the band under Variants).

lines.name: Schneckenband (fusee band, complete)
lines.fn: The band with its two hooks brazed on (1.3.43): the page's Variants.

lines.name: Band (fusee band)
lines.fn: The strip, 0.22 thick, between the barrel and the fusee.

lines.name: Bandhaken rund (band's round hook)
lines.fn: On the fusee's pin.

lines.name: Bandhaken f. Trommel (band's drum hook)
lines.fn: In the drum's slot.

lines.name: Minutenrohr (cannon tube)
lines.fn: Pressed on the centre arbor's 1:80 shank, held by three punched dents in its groove pressed into the shank's groove under it (05 05 03's "Körner": the dents estimated): its foot is the cannon pinion (14 leaves, m 0.36), which drives the change wheel; its square carries the minute hand (no sheet of its own: 05 05 03 gives it).

lines.name: Wechselrad kompl. (change wheel complete)
lines.fn: The motion work's change wheel, its pipe and pinion (28.2.41).

lines.name: Wechselrad (change wheel)
lines.fn: Riveted on its pipe; the cannon pinion drives it.

lines.name: Wechselbutzen (change wheel pipe)
lines.fn: Runs on the short stud (Laufsitz auf Anrichtstift), its foot on the stud bush.

lines.name: Wechseltrieb (change pinion)
lines.fn: Knocked on the pipe to a press fit; drives the hour wheel (no sheet in the set).

lines.name: Stundenrad kompl. (hour wheel complete)
lines.fn: The hour wheel riveted on its pipe (20.7.40).

lines.name: Stundenrad (hour wheel)
lines.fn: Riveted on its pipe; the change pinion drives it.

lines.name: Stundenbutzen (hour wheel pipe)
lines.fn: Runs on the cannon tube, over the cannon pinion; carries the hour hand on its tapered seat (no sheet of its own: 05 02 03 gives it).

lines.name: Auf u. Abrad kompl. (up-and-down wheel complete)
lines.fn: The up-and-down wheel riveted on its pipe (27.2.41).

lines.name: Auf u. Abrad (up-and-down wheel)
lines.fn: Riveted on its pipe; the up-and-down pinion on the fusee arbor drives it.

lines.name: Auf u. Abrad-Butzen (up-and-down wheel pipe)
lines.fn: Runs on the long stud (Laufsitz auf Anrichtstift), its foot on the stud bush; carries the up-and-down hand.

lines.name: Auf u. Abtrieb (up-and-down pinion)
lines.fn: Pressed on the fusee arbor's dial-side end (the fusee group's): drives the up-and-down wheel (no sheet in the set; numbered by the coloured section's label).

lines.name: Minutenzeiger (minute hand)
lines.fn: Pressed on the cannon tube's square, its square hole (2,6 H7, Kegel 1:70) on the square's 2,6 r6 (05 05 03), down on the square's shoulder.

lines.name: Stundenzeiger (hour hand)
lines.fn: On the hour wheel's pipe's tapered seat.

lines.name: Auf u. Abzeiger (up-and-down hand)
lines.fn: On the up-and-down wheel's pipe's seat, down on its shoulder.

lines.name: Sekundenzeiger (seconds hand)
lines.fn: On its collet.

lines.name: Zeigerfutter (seconds hand collet)
lines.fn: Pressed on the seconds arbor's post through the dial; the hand riveted on its end (no sheet in the set; numbered by the coloured section's label).

lines.name: Zifferblatt (dial)
lines.fn: In the movement ring's recess, placed by its pin, held by three screws.

lines.name: Schraube (dial screw)
lines.fn: M1 through the dial's sunk holes into the ring's flange (WN-10 by the coloured section's label, likely).

lines.name: Stift (dial pin)
lines.fn: In the ring's pin hole at 6 deg past 12 (05 08 00-3), stepped into the dial's (no number read).

lines.name: Stellstift 3 (WN-202): the movement ring’s radial pin to the case
lines.fn: Stands 1.78 out of the ring's flange at 12 o'clock into the notch in the bowl's threaded rim: it sets the movement's turn in the case and holds it while the bezel is screwed down.

lines.name: Gehäusetopf (bowl)
lines.fn: The cast brass bowl: the movement ring's flange in a rebate in its rim, the rim threaded outside for the bezel and notched for the ring's pin; the winding hole in its bottom over the fusee's square.

lines.name: Gehäusekloben (case bracket)
lines.fn: On the bowl at 12 and 6 o'clock, carrying the inner pivots; slid along its slots to level the bowl.

lines.name: Feststellkloben (locking bracket)
lines.fn: On the bowl at 50 deg from 6 o'clock: the transit lock presses the ring onto it.

lines.name: Schraube WN-78 (13 on 05 01): the brackets’ screws
lines.fn: Hold the case brackets and the locking bracket to the bowl, M4 (the case brackets', heads Ø 7) and M2.5, 3.3 into its 4 wall (length estimated); their tapped holes across the turned bowl not cut (embed: the thread measured inside the bowl's metal).

lines.name: Bracket screws (6MX)
lines.fn: Hold the Soviet 6MX's high case brackets (two each, in slots) and its locking bracket (two, in its vertical slot) to the bowl, their holes across the turned bowl not cut. No sheet: Kirov No. 247's bowl (12_Kirow_247_E-Kontakt_3.jpg).

lines.name: Verschlußplatte (closing plate)
lines.fn: In the bowl's foot, turning on its screw to open and shut the winding hole.

lines.name: Schraube WN-71 (7 on 05 01, the number unsure): the closing plate’s screw
lines.fn: The screw in the bowl's bottom the closing plate turns on.

lines.name: Schraube WN-72: the closing plate’s knob
lines.fn: The knob in the closing plate's M2.6, to turn it.

lines.name: Verschlußfeder (closing spring)
lines.fn: Holds the closing plate shut over the winding hole and turns it back when the key is out: a wire spiral in the plate's groove, one end in the plate's Ø 1.2, the other in the bowl's bottom (no sheet: estimated from the plate's; its ends sit free in their holes, so no relation is measured).

lines.name: Glasrand (bezel)
lines.fn: Screws onto the bowl's threaded rim round the movement ring's flange, its step on the dial holding the movement down; the glass in its top.

lines.name: Glas (glass)
lines.fn: In the bezel's top, flush with it.

lines.name: Kardanring (gimbal ring)
lines.fn: Between the bowl and the box: its outer pivots in the box's walls, its inner pivots in the bowl's brackets.

lines.name: Kardanringkloben (ring bracket)
lines.fn: On the ring at 3 o'clock, carrying that outer pivot; slid along its slots to level the bowl.

lines.name: Schraube (the ring bracket’s screws, no number)
lines.fn: Hold the ring bracket to the ring: through its holes, tapped through the ring to its inside, as 05 01 Schnitt A-B draws them (cut along the radius; 2.75 into it until 27 October 2026).

lines.name: Schraube WN-79 (12 on 05 01): the inner pivots
lines.fn: Through the ring at 12 and 6 o'clock (M5, tapped in it), their plain tips the inner pivots in the case brackets' holes (05 01 Schnitt C-D).

lines.name: Kontermutter WN-400 (10 on 05 01), knurled brass
lines.fn: Lock the inner pivot screws where they are set: inside the ring, against its inner face (05 01 Schnitt C-D: Ø 22 × 2.4).

lines.name: Holzkasten (wooden box)
lines.fn: 185 x 185 x 180 outside: the gimbals hang in it (no sheet in the set).

lines.name: Schraube WN-80 (11 on 05 01): the outer pivots, M6
lines.fn: Through the box's side walls, their tips the gimbal ring's pivots: through the ring at 9 o'clock, through its bracket into the ring at 3 (05 01's elevation).

lines.name: Bearing disc (no number)
lines.fn: On each side wall's inside round the outer pivot.

lines.name: Griff f. Chronometerkasten (handle)
lines.fn: On each side, under the pivot, over the wall's finger recess (an oval 70 × 30, 10 deep in the 12.5 wall).

lines.name: Schraube (the handles’ screws, estimated)
lines.fn: Through the handles' ends into the side walls.

lines.name: Scharnier (piano hinge, estimated)
lines.fn: Join the lid to the box at the back: one hinge 148 long, its leaves let into the parting faces (as every photographed box).

lines.name: Deckelstütze (lid stay, estimated)
lines.fn: Holds the lid open: a slotted brass bar pivoted on the lid's left wall, riding on a pin in the box's (Wempe 6161).

lines.name: Schlüsselhalter (key holder, estimated)
lines.fn: A shelf across the box's back right corner, its front edge curved round the gimbal ring (Wempe 6161, 3044; 51-00_1 draws a triangle), the winding key standing in a round fitting on it, its tube down through the shelf.

lines.name: Fassung (the key holder's round fitting, estimated)
lines.fn: A round brass cup standing on the shelf (51-00_1's circle; Lange VEB 2285's, on its shelf): the key's cone seats on its bore.

lines.name: Schraube (the key holder's fitting's screws, estimated)
lines.fn: Through the fitting into the shelf, either side of the key (51-00_1's two dots).

lines.name: Holzschraube DIN 96, 3 × 15 (the transit lock's bracket's wood screws, estimated)
lines.fn: Round-headed wood screws through the bracket's wall leg into the box's right wall (the owner's case design, CAD Model Case.md §10: 2 × 3 × 15 DIN 96).

lines.name: Schließblech (keeper, estimated)
lines.fn: On the box's front: the latch tongue's end goes under it.

lines.name: Pin over the outer pivot (no number; inferred a lid-locating pin)
lines.fn: Standing 2.3 out of each side wall's parting face over its outer pivot, into a hole in the closed lid's wall (05 01's elevation draws it; its purpose inferred).

lines.name: Deckel (the box’s lid)
lines.fn: The glazed lid, hinged at the back.

lines.name: Deckelglas (the lid’s glass, estimated)
lines.fn: In the lid's top, under its frame.

lines.name: Firmenschild (maker’s plate), Type 3371
lines.fn: On the lid's front.

lines.name: Zunge (latch tongue)
lines.fn: Turning on its screw on the lid's front, its end under the keeper (its place estimated).

lines.name: Schraube (the tongue’s pivot screw, estimated)
lines.fn: The screw the tongue turns on.

lines.name: Knopf (the tongue’s knob, estimated)
lines.fn: In the tongue's M3.5.

lines.name: Überkasten (outer box): body and base plate, bleached birch
lines.fn: Carries the wooden box for transport, cushioned all round.

lines.name: Leiste (rim strip, 17, 18)
lines.fn: Inside the rim, 4 over the walls: the lid closes over it.

lines.name: Polster (front and back cushions)
lines.fn: Against the wooden box's front and back.

lines.name: Polster (end cushions)
lines.fn: Against the wooden box's handles.

lines.name: Polster (floor cushion)
lines.fn: The wooden box stands on it.

lines.name: Riemen (strap, 10): its ends on the end walls
lines.fn: Over the lid to its buckle (its loose ends and buckle not drawn).

lines.name: Schraube f. Riemenbef. (the strap's screws)
lines.fn: Two on each end wall, 80 apart.

lines.name: Öse (eye, 12)
lines.fn: On each end of the base plate.

lines.name: Schraube 3 x 15 DIN 96 (11)
lines.fn: The eyes' screws.

lines.name: Scharnier (outer box hinge, 7)
lines.fn: Join the lid to the body at the back.

lines.name: Öse (the hook's eye, 9: commercial)
lines.fn: On the front, under the rim.

lines.name: Deckel (the outer box's lid)
lines.fn: Hinged at the back, cushioned inside.

lines.name: Polster (lid cushion, 16)
lines.fn: Bears on the wooden box's lid.

lines.name: Haken (hook, 9: commercial)
lines.fn: On the lid's front, caught in the eye.

lines.name: Ящик (the 6MX’s box, Kirov No. 247’s): its body
lines.fn: 190 x 190 x 190 outside (the TU's): the gimbals hang in it. No sheet: Kirov 247's photographs, its tiers on Kirov 22823's.

lines.name: Hinges (6MX, estimated)
lines.fn: Join the glazed lid to the box at the back, and the top lid to it (not seen on Kirov 247's photographs).

lines.name: Ring handle (6MX)
lines.fn: One on each side, under the lower parting line.

lines.name: Corner strips (6MX)
lines.fn: Brass strips round the box's corners (the lids' with them).

lines.name: Hasp leaf (6MX)
lines.fn: Two hasps across the parting lines, a knurled screw on each lower leaf.

lines.name: Number plate 247 (6MX)
lines.fn: On the box's front and the outer box's lid.

lines.name: Glazed lid and top lid (6MX)
lines.fn: Hinged at the back, opened together here.

lines.name: Factory badge, 1 МЧЗ им. Кирова (6MX)
lines.fn: On the glazed lid's front.

lines.name: Outer box (6MX): its body
lines.fn: Carries the box for transport, felt-lined; its sizes estimated.

lines.name: Felt (6MX)
lines.fn: Under, round and over the box.

lines.name: Outer box lid (6MX)
lines.fn: Hinged at the back, its tab closing into the notch.

lines.name: Feststeller (transit lock)
lines.fn: A knob and lever in the box's front right corner: turned in, the lever presses the ring onto the locking bracket.

lines.name: Schlüsselgriff (key handle)
lines.fn: The key's round flat paddle.

lines.name: Schlüsselmittelteil (key body)
lines.fn: The key's black steel body.

lines.name: Schlüsselrohr (key tube)
lines.fn: The brass tube with the square socket.

lines.name: Wendelfeder (the key’s coil spring)
lines.fn: Round the tube in the body's bore: it grips the tube one way and slips the other.

lines.name: Kerbstift K.S. 1 (the key’s grooved pin)
lines.fn: Through the body and the paddle.

lines.name: Körper (the 1940 key's body, with its collar)
lines.fn: The conical body of the key of 1940 (Aufzugschlüssel 127-556.02 U 01, the page's Variants, As first drawn).

lines.name: Griff (the 1940 key's flat pear-shaped handle, its tang)
lines.fn: The handle, a flat plate, its tang in the body.

lines.name: Schaft (the 1940 key's stem, with the socket for the fusee's square)
lines.fn: Pressed into the body; its socket takes the fusee's winding square.

lines.name: Schraube (the 1940 key's screw beside the tang)
lines.fn: On the collar beside the tang (its click spring 127-556.02-04 not drawn).

lines.name: Contact base (6MX, Romanov's 58)

lines.name: Insulation (6MX, 68)
lines.fn: Black fibre under each contact block, insulating it from the base. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Contact block + (6MX, 52)

lines.name: Contact block − (6MX, 57)

lines.name: Insulating bush (6MX, 67)
lines.fn: Insulates each block screw from its block, its black flange under the head. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Contact block screw (6MX)
lines.fn: Hold the blocks and their insulation to the base: steel cheese heads Ø 3.1. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Contact disc (6MX, 55)
lines.fn: The knurled gilt disc the contact screw meets, upright on its bracket on block 57; it may be turned to renew a burnt contact (the 6MX's instruction). No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Contact lever staff (6MX, 69)
lines.fn: The lever's staff, jewelled at both ends; the spiral's collet on it. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Contact staff's upper jewel setting (6MX)
lines.fn: Holds the staff's upper hole jewel and end jewel in the base. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Hole jewel (6MX), contact staff, upper

lines.name: End jewel (6MX), contact staff, upper
lines.fn: The staff's upper end stone. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Contact cock (6MX)
lines.fn: The L-shaped gilt cock over the spiral, holding the staff's lower jewels. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Contact cock screw (6MX)
lines.fn: Holds the cock's foot to the base. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Contact cock steady pin (6MX)

lines.name: Hole jewel (6MX), contact staff, lower

lines.name: Contact cock's cap plate (6MX)
lines.fn: Holds the staff's lower end jewel on the cock's arm. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: End jewel (6MX), contact staff, lower

lines.name: Cap plate screw (6MX)
lines.fn: Hold the cap plate to the cock's arm. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Contact lever (6MX, 60)

lines.name: Contact spring screw (6MX, 65)
lines.fn: Hold the springs' feet through the bowl's wall, slotted brass heads outside (their holes across the turned bowl not cut). No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Contact terminal (6MX)
lines.fn: A brass socket outside the bowl for each lead, marked + and − on the bowl. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.

lines.name: Terminal washer (6MX, 63)
lines.fn: Black fibre washers under the springs' screws and the terminals outside the bowl. No sheet: the Soviet 6MX's electrical contact (Kirov No. 247's photographs by Johannes Altmeppen; Romanov 1975, Figs. 100-101 and p. 105's parts list), its sizes estimated where the photographs don't give them.
